title: Wagertech <> Jumpr: Weekly Sync

items.statement: Emily asked to nail down the approach for the partner/operator/country/market reference list and the unique ID for each value. The meeting did not come back to this topic.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I don't know if Joyce had a chance to look through the kind of um the partner operator country market like list that you created. we should just kind of nail down like the approach that you took there and the IDs

items.statement: Kobi showed the sign-up record combined into two columns: player information/details on one side and end-user entry fields on the other. Full tabs are not possible across the board; Kobi offered to switch the column order if the client prefers.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I was able to combine uh the interface into just the two columns ... we we can't do the full tab across the board ... Uh the order of which you can tell me like we can always switch it around. / Joyce Kiddell: This is looking so much better.

items.topic: New status read-only for end users
items.statement: In New status the sign-up record is read-only for end users; editing needs admin or a permission. Reps only have the two buttons, including the log sign-up action that moves the record to In Progress.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Nothing on this screen would be um editable though, right? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Correct. Yeah, / Kobi Kunasekaran: So none of this is going to be editable by uh an end user. Um so you need to have like you need to be an admin or have the permissions to be able to edit these fields. Um so read only except for the two buttons, right? They can click on lock signup.
items.asr_note: lock signup = log signup [ASR?] (Kobi says "log signup" at line 195)

items.topic: In Progress screen proofs and history
items.statement: In In Progress the screen shows proof and deposit info and referral info; a history tab shows multiple clicks; player information is not editable because automation sets it. Kobi asked the client to say if any field is missing.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Once we go into in progress, the screen changes. ... we have the proof and deposit info and the referral info. ... But if there's anything missing, let me know. ... over here we have the history tab just shows the history of clicks. ... the player information u they can't really edit because this is already like set through the automations behind the scenes when the uh clicks come in um but they can add in the proofs.

items.statement: Proof status counts up as proofs are entered, but completion logic is not updated. Jumpr is waiting on the final field set and the open-questions answer on what counts as completion.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I haven't uh updated the completion logic. I think we're still waiting on finalizing the field set in the open questions out for what one all is considered uh completion.

items.statement: Kobi added the no-refer field Emily asked for; when checked, the other two referral fields disappear.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I had noted to add the no refer and as like a variable within completion and I think it was there, right? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. So, I added the no refer field here. So, if they do check no refer, then the other two fields disappear.

items.topic: No secondary referrer when no refer
items.statement: Lina confirmed that when no refer is checked there is no secondary referrer.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think you still want the secondary refer though, right? Or is like is it all like no referral at all? / Lina Ceniccola: If it's no refer then we wouldn't have secondary

items.statement: Lina asked how hard it is to add one more field to the referral information section (field not yet known). Kobi said adding a field to the layout is easy, but any behavior tied to it (for example with no referral checked) needs scoping.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: would it be to add a field within the referral information section? Like say we needed to add just one extra thing. / Kobi Kunasekaran: it's the behavior that you want you want tied to that uh field that's where the effort goes in. So like if if you need that field to you know, in a particular state when the no referral is checked that like we'd have to scope that out to see what that is,

items.statement: Lina asked to add back the notes section in referral information; Kobi agreed. Waleed confirmed the notes are for the specific sign-up, not the referral in general.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Cuz we also had a note section and referral information. I don't see that here anymore. Can we add that back? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh we can yeah just like just do you want to call it like refer notes or just regular notes? Okay. Yeah, / Kobi Kunasekaran: we can add that / Waleed Alasadi: So it's notes for this particular signup, right? Like it's not just for the referral in general. / Lina Ceniccola: Yes.

items.statement: Emily asked to move the secondary referral down because payout type and amount link to the primary referrer. Kobi said "Yeah" and moved on to the payout automation; no explicit change confirmed.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: And then the only other like small but can we bring the secondary referral like down because the payout is just so that the like refer payout / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Emily Vandenberg: type and uh payment amount are all linked to the primary.

items.statement: Payout amount is automated: choosing cash fills it from the referral matrix the client sent, driven by the sign-up currency. Referral currency is displayed; sign-up currency is in the admin More Info tab.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And actually the pay payout amount um we actually set this up so that there is some automation. ... if I choose cash, um it'll fill it out based on that matrix that you sent us. So depending on the currency of the signup itself ... I am displaying the referral currency

items.statement: Lina confirmed the referral currency must stay visible because it decides which bank (Canadian or US) pays the referral.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, definitely want to keep the referral currency because that changes which platform they pay / Lina Ceniccola: out the referral. So just at like a quick glance, they know, okay, I'm going to pay this from the Canadian bank. / Lina Ceniccola: It's the US bank. So they definitely want access to that info.

items.statement: Lina will try to get Jumpr the referral information and settle an internal workflow question on secondary referrers as soon as possible; she does not expect changes now. Kobi asked to be told if anything on the matrix changes.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Um I'll try to get you the referral information. / Lina Ceniccola: I don't think we'll have any changes at this time, ... we might just internally change like how we view secondary referers. / Kobi Kunasekaran: for this one, yeah, let me know if like anything on the matrix uh changes.

items.statement: Jumpr has not built automation for the secondary referral (planned on the referral object); Kobi said it does not block this phase, so a client change there costs no rework.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. I we haven't added any automations around the secondary referral yet. Um because that that was supposed to be mostly on the referral object as opposed to the signup. So, uh, it doesn't seem to be blocking for this phase yet,

items.statement: Operator logos now display. Logos for about 60-70 operators must be filled in for go-live (upload to Salesforce, ops paste the image URL); Kobi said the teams may need to work together on how.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, as you can see, we I was able to get the um logo added in as well for some of the operators. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, um I we may need to work together to figure out how to fill in get like the lo logos and fill it in for every single operator when when we're going live. ... you do just have to upload the logo into Salesforce. Um, and as ops paste in the URL for that image from Salesforce

items.statement: Canada and US country icons display; per-state emojis are not possible, so state stays as text.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: for the country, um, we were able to get the Canada and US as well. So um the the logo show for state uh I don't think we can really do any uh emojis for each individual state. So that's still going to remain as text.

items.statement: Kobi asked the client to give the icons they want for verticals, if they want them; Jumpr can then add them.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: and for vertical uh I think I left a comment for this. Um if you want to give me the icons that you'd like to use to separate these ones uh we can easily add those in as well.

items.statement: Emily asked about showing market in the split-view queue; Lina suggested a market filter, then asked for a sort by market. Kobi said market is two fields and they can sort by country.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Can we just do a sort by market? / Kobi Kunasekaran: We can um but market is two fields though. Um do we want to combine this into a single field somehow just / Lina Ceniccola: country. / Kobi Kunasekaran: yeah we can.

items.statement: Waleed suggested a country flag next to the player name in the list; Emily and Lina agreed, and Kobi confirmed it will show the Canadian or US flag next to the name.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: but can we add the flag next to the name like E2E tester like Canada? / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: that's something we can do. Like next to like Jake Morrison, it will just be either the Canadian flag or the US flag.

items.statement: Lina asked to color the whole row red for fraud instead of the red flag emoji. Kobi said no; the list shows up to four fields in a chosen order.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: I'm talking about red flags to make it red highlight. / Lina Ceniccola: what if you just had it all colored red? Is that possible? Similar to how you have that red banner for fraud. / Kobi Kunasekaran: No, / Lina Ceniccola: No. Okay.

items.topic: Move red fraud flag next to name
items.statement: Joyce asked to move the red fraud flag to the immediate right of the person's name; Kobi said they can rearrange. The client then said it would sit with the list view before deciding the final look.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So, what if is it possible to at least move the red flag to the right, like the more immediate right of the person's name? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Yeah, we can do that. We can rearrange like some of these if it'll be helpful.

items.statement: Lina asked if the list view can follow her screenshot (operator logo with progress/status together, proof status and flags on the right). Kobi said yes, but the date may be lost; Lina said the team will take it away and decide.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: Yeah. And I'm I'm wondering just based on the screenshot that I sent if the format / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think the only one that I like so yes I could do it exactly like that. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, but then we may not have the date. / Lina Ceniccola: if it's possible. Um, just like Will said, we can take that away and determine if that's the move.

items.topic: Client to review list view layout
items.statement: Waleed suggested the client take a day to get used to the list icons; Emily and Lina agreed to sit with it and confirm how they want it to look.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: If I may suggest you guys take like a day to look at it. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, we can kind of sit with / Lina Ceniccola: And then we'll we'll nail it down how we just want it to look

items.statement: Kobi explained the split view shows only the first four fields, in order; formula fields can combine data and icons (e.g. player plus country icon).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But the limitation is four fields and the first four fields um are the ones that show up when we go into the split view. And then obviously the order matters.

items.topic: Drop status text once icons known
items.statement: Kobi suggested removing the status text later, once users know the icons; Lina agreed it is a good point.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Nice. I think like also like once people get used to the icons, we can even remove the text for the status too, right? / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, that's true,

items.statement: Emily confirmed there is no way to filter by market in the split view other than separate list views; table view has user filters but there are no quick filters. Emily will discuss internally.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: And then Kobe, just to confirm, there's no like way that we'll be able to filter outside of creating a separate list view within like the different markets. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Like there's no concept of like quick filters. That that's the whole point of these lists. / Emily Vandenberg: Okay, we can talk about that internally.

items.topic: SLC missing data flagged for review
items.statement: Study link clicks without enough data to create a sign-up are flagged for review; someone fixes the data and a button reprocesses it through the automation. The test record without operator/partner was forced through and should not happen in production.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So those would get so those uh SLC's or uh study link clicks that come in without enough information for us to create the signup record. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um we added like a review review uh process where it'll get flagged for review ... and then we'll have a button to reprocess it through the automation to have it try to link it to an existing signup. That's kind of the plan. / Emily Vandenberg: Okay.

items.statement: Any sign-up flagged as fraud is locked for rep editing regardless of status; ops must uncheck the fraud flag to allow editing again.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So for new yeah we have the the fraud flag um anything that's uh flagged as fraud you'll notice it is locked for editing. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So this these records do need to be unlocked by the ops team. ... if they do need access and ops would need to uncheck that fraud flag so that they can go back to editing it.

items.topic: Sign-ups flagged as fraud at creation
items.statement: Kobi said he had a question about sign-ups flagged for fraud from the start and would come back to it; he did not raise it again in this meeting.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: or if it's flagged right from the get- go which is actually another question I want to ask but I'll come back to it in a second.

items.statement: Archived records are not editable by reps; a Reactivate button returns them to In Progress. The archive and fraud reasons from the open-questions log are added; choosing Other requires more detail.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And then for archive records we added the reactivate button. So, um, if I click on reactivate, um, it'll bring it back to in progress. ... Um, and for archive and fraud, we have the, uh, the new reasons that you provided in the open questions lock. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, and if they choose other, they'll need to provide the additional information.
items.asr_note: open questions lock = open questions log [ASR?]

items.topic: Fraud review status; dismiss automation pending
items.statement: Ops set fraud review status (under review, confirmed, dismissed). The automation that clears the flag and reopens the record on dismiss is not built yet.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: so this is where you know as ops you would come in and you can mark it as under review, confirmed or dismissed. We don't have the automation yet, but when uh when that's live, when you set it to dismiss, it'll basically uncheck this, clear this, clear this, and the record will be opened up for reps

items.topic: Ops keep sign-up edit access for now
items.statement: Kobi offered to lock down ops editing of sign-up fields (partner, deal, operator). Lina asked to leave it editable for ops just in case and tighten it later when confident; Kobi agreed, with edit only for those who need access.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: but you have the option if you want or we can lock it down so nobody has the ability to edit / Lina Ceniccola: Like could we just leave it and then um not edit it if we don't need to, / Lina Ceniccola: but just leave it as we could edit it just in case almost like we don't know what we don't know in this new state. / Lina Ceniccola: And then maybe when we have more confidence, we can just like gray it out / Kobi Kunasekaran: tighten that up. Yeah. Yeah, / Kobi Kunasekaran: I'm good with that. ... But uh yeah, but this is only going to be for whoever needs access. So we can lock it down for everybody except like 10 minutes.

items.asr_note: 'except like 10 minutes' is unclear; possibly 'except admins' [ASR?]

items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: And then I just want to be clear on one thing. The agency signup date that will autofill from the / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, this will come from the player. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Right now, we don't have that feeding in properly yet, but uh it should come from the player based on their first sign / Lina Ceniccola: So, the BA won't um they won't input that data and then the affiliate signup / Kobi Kunasekaran: Correct.

items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So I think this is manually entered right now. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So it is the expectation is that they would enter that in because a click doesn't necessarily mean that they actually signed up,

items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: We can re label that for sure if needed, but the / Lina Ceniccola: Yeah, just sign up date to be / Lina Ceniccola: honest. Sign up date. Sign up proof. Deposit date proof and then / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yep.

items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: the agency site sign up date or agency registration date. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Oh yeah, actually that registration is a good one because they register for an / Lina Ceniccola: Do you guys agree with that? / Owen Scott: Yeah, I agree with / Jay: Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I can can make that change. Easy

items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: is that necessary for phase one, / Lina Ceniccola: Yes. Yes, it / Lina Ceniccola: is. / Kobi Kunasekaran: deposit amount is like the allocated amount and then the actual amount is what they actually deposit and we want the ability for them to enter that information in. Yeah, we can do that. ... I can add a checkbox below. If they check it, then another field shows up to put in the actual deposit amount.

items.statement: Kobi showed the deal rep view: operator, partner, market, country at top, read-only; related lists cut to deal assignments and sign-ups. The More Info config tab (CPA, commissions, redeposit ranges) is for admins but is not yet hidden from reps.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, operator, partner, market, country. So, this is the rep view. Um right, I'm logged in as a rep. This is all I can see. Um I can't edit anything here. ... Um, the more info tab, it's not hidden for reps right now, but this they wouldn't have access to this. It'll only be for admins.

items.topic: Manage deal assignment button in Salesforce
items.statement: Kobi showed admins/ops/managers assigning a deal to reps with an effective date and ending it with an effective end date; he noted the effective-from date must be kept on update. (Later in the meeting, assignment moved to the CMS.)
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: as uh admins, you can go in or admins or ops or managers, you can go in and if you want to assign this uh deal over to uh reps, pick the rep active, set a date of when this assignment will be effective, save, and then it'll create the assignments for you. ... I guess we need to make sure that it keeps the effective from uh we'll take care of that.

items.statement: Kobi said the concatenated deal name is long and asked the client for a shorthand for partners/operators. Lina said she does not mind the long title and the four deal parts at the top are key.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, we might need a better way to represent the deal instead of just the deal ID. Um, I want to like leave this with you to see if uh there's like a shorthand / Lina Ceniccola: I don't hate the long title. in terms of deal and Owen could probably speak more to this, but I think like I think capturing those like four pieces of information at the top is key.

So, it's always one study per partner or

items.statement: Lina asked if reps can see their given volume and progress against target. Kobi said Jumpr could add a manager-set target field on deal assignment and count related sign-ups against it; Owen said this covers the deal needs.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: And are we able to include like what volume they've been given and for them to see how they've how much they've completed for their target? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh we could add that in into the dealer assignment uh object as additional fields. / Kobi Kunasekaran: we could have another field to set like target uh for each one. / Owen Scott: Yeah, I can't think of anything else right now that I'd need, but that basically covers everything from a deal perspective.

items.statement: Emily said the CMS working session changes where Salesforce owns input and must send information to the CMS, which is not built into the current scope. Kobi later said nothing goes from Salesforce to the CMS today and that side may be a bigger build.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: where Salesforce is going to receive information versus where we're going to where it's going to kind of own the input and send have to send information to the CMS because we don't have that built into the scope right / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, we have to figure that out because we don't have any uh anything going out from Salesforce into CMS today. So, that might actually be a little bit of a bigger build than the other way

items.topic: Deal config in SF, pushed to CMS
items.statement: Deal details and operator links are managed in Salesforce. When a deal is published it is sent to the CMS, where it appears as a dropdown option when ops assign a link to a rep.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So, at the highest level, our goal is to um manage the details of a deal um still within Salesforce. Um, and that includes, you know, everything that's on the screen as well as the, um, links that we receive directly from our operators. / Joyce Kiddell: Um and then uh once we publish a deal then it should trigger that being sent to the CMS and anyone in the CMS um who goes to add a link to a rep will have that deal as an option to choose from um in like a drop-own list. So the actual rep assignment happens on the CMS

items.statement: Deal rep assignments will be made in the CMS, not with the Salesforce Manage Deal Assignment button; Salesforce only displays what the CMS sends. Kobi said he had understood it the other way around.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So you're saying Joyce that we're not going to click manage up assignment in Salesforce. It's just going to display what assignments you've made in the CMS. / Joyce Kiddell: Correct. Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh, okay. Just to make sure, I thought I understood it the other way around. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Mhm. Okay. So they then they don't necessarily need to manage the assignments from Salesforce, right? Like this is just a visual layer. / Joyce Kiddell: That's correct.
items.supersedes_hint: Replaces the earlier design where reps were assigned to deals in Salesforce via the Manage Deal Assignment button
items.asr_note: manage up assignment = manage deal assignment [ASR?]

items.topic: CMS pushes assignments back to SF
items.statement: When an assignment happens in the CMS it pushes back to Salesforce, with history, so reporting can track rep performance against the deal.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: And it will have to like history. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, like it'll still push back into Salesforce once the uh assignment happens so that we can still close the loop like you said around um you know if a rep is assigned to a specific deal, how are they trending against that with the signups

items.statement: Links are configured as a list at deal level in Salesforce, not pre-assigned per rep; in the CMS ops pick from the deal's links when assigning a rep. Emily had pictured it differently but accepted.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: originally I was thinking it would just be like the list of all of the available links under that deal is configured at a deal level and then when you go into the CMS EMS you just pick from the drop down / Joyce Kiddell: We would still do that. It would just happen on the CMS side instead of pre- assigning links to reps in the Salesforce. / Emily Vandenberg: Okay. Yeah, whatever you whatever you decide. I was I was thinking of it differently, but

items.statement: The deal page needs a place to add affiliate tracking links with the ability to turn each on and off; the rep link slug field is not needed on the deal.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: No, we we don't need that here. / Joyce Kiddell: It's um on the deal page itself. We'll just need to have a spot where we can add the affiliate tracking links. / Joyce Kiddell: we just need the ability to turn it off and on.

items.statement: Joyce said deactivating a link deal-wide happens in Salesforce and inactive-link flow to the CMS still needs thought. Owen asked that link changes (including shutting off a link) be done in the CMS with Salesforce tracking them; Lina summarized that link changes stay in the CMS. Not settled.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: And in the first option, if you're just like deactivating that link altogether, I feel like that has to happen in Salesforce / Joyce Kiddell: if it's inactive, we got to think through that flow a bit. / Owen Scott: Just general things like shutting off a link, / Lina Ceniccola: connected, but you you're making like the action of changing links and whatnot still lives in the CMS.

items.topic: Affiliate link child object and API
items.statement: Kobi proposed a new child object for affiliate links (like deal assignments) with a button to create each link, tied to an API callout to the CMS once the callout is defined. Joyce accepted.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we we can create another object u like a child object similar to how we have the deal assignments. / Kobi Kunasekaran: and then we'll as once we finalize what that call out looks like to CMS, / Joyce Kiddell: Perfect. / Kobi Kunasekaran: we would have that tied to uh tied to an API allowed to send that payload over.

items.statement: Salesforce will not enforce rules such as a link belonging to only one rep; the CMS must, and Salesforce can surface errors. Joyce accepted.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um but we won't be able to do any guardrails from the Salesforce side to enforce that you know a rep can only have uh like a link can only belong to one rep u or things like that like you'll have to do that on the CMS side like we can surface errors / Joyce Kiddell: That's okay.

items.statement: Owen asked to make link and deal changes in the CMS. Joyce said the CMS has no deal management, so ops must create each deal in Salesforce to make it a CMS option; Salesforce still tracks changes. Owen accepted.
items.quote: Owen Scott: I think in terms of changing links or changing deals or doing anything related to that. I think that should all be in the CMS / Joyce Kiddell: The ch the challenge with that Owen is that there's no concept of deal management / Joyce Kiddell: you have to be the one to kind of create each deal in Salesforce so that there's like an option for you to choose from / Owen Scott: Sorry. That makes perfect sense.

items.statement: Salesforce replaces AirTable for deal information, including volume targets; deal data added in Salesforce is pushed automatically to the CMS.
items.quote: Lina Ceniccola: So, if I'm understanding correctly, Air Table goes away, Salesforce becomes like the more robust solution for tracking all of our deal information. / Joyce Kiddell: This way, if you um add stuff into Salesforce instead of Air Table, it's going to automatically get pushed over to the CMS.

items.statement: Kobi said the current split is a balance for Phase 1, and the client could later converge on one system (e.g. CMS creates deal config and passes it to Salesforce) to remove the manual step.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I will add that like we could work towards uh converging both into one system eventually too, right? like this is a great actually good balance of making this work uh for phase one but eventually you could uh focus on one system to take on more of the management

items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: I I'm assuming it's not built already in your CMS. Is that correct? / Joyce Kiddell: It is / Joyce Kiddell: built. / Joyce Kiddell: And that's where like we haven't built out the API for this yet, but uh that'll be critical in ensuring that like those two records or systems talk to each other.

items.topic: CMS creates/updates deal assignments via API
items.statement: Deal assignments are the critical link between deals and reps for metrics. The CMS will create and update deal assignment records in Salesforce through an API callout with required fields.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: would you be able to like create and manage the deal / Waleed Alasadi: assignment records from the CMS because we'll need those to be created here and then updated, / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, for sure. / Waleed Alasadi: when you create an assignment in the CMS we're going to need an API call out to Salesforce to create like this deal assignment record with these required fields and then when that is / Waleed Alasadi: updated then that's what we're going to need to see as well.

items.topic: Jumpr to send API requirements doc
items.statement: Jumpr will accelerate and send a requirements doc for the CMS-to-Salesforce deal assignment API. Joyce asked for it ASAP; WagerTech could start on it later this week.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: So maybe we should just from our end like accelerate the API requirements. / Joyce Kiddell: Mhm. That'd be great. / Waleed Alasadi: we can we can give you the requirements choice / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Yeah. if you want to shoot over a doc with that. / Joyce Kiddell: if you can get us that doc um ASAP for the starting
items.due: ASAP; WagerTech may start later this week

items.topic: API before data migration this week
items.statement: Both the API and historical data migration are go-live blockers, but for this week WagerTech will prioritize the deal assignment API over data migration.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Great. Yeah. And would you say this takes um priority probably over the historical data? Okay. / Waleed Alasadi: They're both well I think they're both like go live blockers right like one / Joyce Kiddell: We'll do both, but I'm just wondering like in terms of by end of week, what what would you prioritize? / Waleed Alasadi: The this this stuff, not the not the not the data migration.

items.statement: If the API is not ready for go-live, Waleed said the team can discuss using the existing Salesforce deal assignment until it is ready.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: is if the this the manual I guess or the Salesforce deal assignment it's built / Waleed Alasadi: already so if the API is not completed by time for go live we can discuss using the assignment in Salesforce until such time it is ready

items.topic: Data migration needed for day one
items.statement: Waleed said data migration is needed so reps exist and see their data from day one.
items.quote: Waleed Alasadi: Um, and then the the data migration is also necessary for your reps to be there and see it from day / Waleed Alasadi: one.

items.topic: UAT this week; migration next week
items.statement: Kobi said, assuming the team is ready to go into UAT this week, data migration and spreadsheets can be worked on over the next week.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: assuming like we're ready to go go into UAT this week, that means we can always work on the data migration. and flushing out the spreadsheets over the next week, right?

items.statement: Jumpr will define what WagerTech sends in payloads, but Jumpr needs WagerTech's input on what the CMS needs from Salesforce and how authentication works. Joyce agreed it is the grayer part and will prioritize it.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Like we need information on what uh you need from Salesforce sent over to CMS and what that authentication and everything looks like. / Joyce Kiddell: This one feels definitely more gray. So, um happy to prioritize it first.

items.statement: Joyce said WagerTech still owes feedback on the rest of the screens and will provide it this week.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I think we still owe you some feedback on like the rest of the screens. / Joyce Kiddell: Um so we can get to that for sure this week.

items.statement: Kobi said sign-up and rep assignment screens are probably good enough for go-live, but the fields to show for players, operators and partners are not defined; he suggested the teams look at it this week and prep before go-live.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, um I this is probably still good enough to go live with. the player information we haven't really touched on like what are all the fields that you want to see for players / Kobi Kunasekaran: So I think this one maybe uh we should like take a look this week as well um and prep before go live.

items.topic: External ID for SLC processing offline
items.statement: The external ID question for study click link processing continues offline using the shared spreadsheet.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: the study click link processing. Um I think we we have that spreadsheet where we're trying to figure out the external ID situation. So as we we'll continue the conversation uh offline with those and try to move that along

items.statement: Kobi reported a milestone on Friday: the team was able to send records over (system direction not stated).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh but we we hit a pretty good milestone on Friday where we were able to uh send those records over.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: The team approved a 2-column layout for lead details ... The team agreed on a two-column structure that separates read-only lead details from editable end-user fields.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh the order of which you can tell me like we can always switch it around. / Joyce Kiddell: This is looking so much better.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer: no one explicitly approved the layout; Kobi left the order open and the client gave only general praise.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: established automated logic for fraud and archive statuses.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: We don't have the automation yet, but when uh when that's live, when you set it to dismiss, it'll basically uncheck this, clear this, clear this
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer: the fraud-dismiss automation is not built yet.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Administrative access was restricted to prevent accidental data changes ... Lina Ceniccola and Emily Vandenberg agreed that while operations may eventually require full editing capabilities, it is safer to restrict access for standard users.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Lina Ceniccola: but just leave it as we could edit it just in case almost like we don't know what we don't know in this new state. / Lina Ceniccola: And then maybe when we have more confidence, we can just like gray it out
gemini_disagreements.why: Inverted: client chose to keep ops edit access now and restrict later; restriction was not the decision. (The Decisions bullet 'Operations editing functionality maintained' matches the transcript.)

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Red flag icon repositioned The red flag icon will be repositioned to the immediate right of the person's name in the UI.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Waleed Alasadi: If I may suggest you guys take like a day to look at it. / Lina Ceniccola: And then we'll we'll nail it down how we just want it to look
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer: Kobi said it can be done, but the client said it would sit with the list view and decide the final look.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: System architecture for deal management defined The team established that the CMS will serve as the interface for managing links and deals, while Salesforce will replace AirTable as the backend system of record.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Joyce Kiddell: The ch the challenge with that Owen is that there's no concept of deal management / Joyce Kiddell: you have to be the one to kind of create each deal in Salesforce so that there's like an option for you to choose from
gemini_disagreements.why: Contradicted: deals are created and configured in Salesforce, not managed in the CMS; only rep link assignment happens in the CMS. Where deal-wide link deactivation happens was not settled.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [Lina Ceniccola] Finalize Referral Matrix: Determine and submit the final referral matrix data to ensure accurate platform payout logic.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Lina Ceniccola: Um I'll try to get you the referral information. / Lina Ceniccola: I don't think we'll have any changes at this time
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer/reframed: Lina said she would try to get referral information and settle a secondary-referrer workflow; she expected no changes and did not commit to submitting a final matrix.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [The group] Update Operator Logos: Gather and provide the logos for all 60 to 70 operators. Upload the image URLs into Salesforce.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, um I we may need to work together to figure out how to fill in get like the lo logos and fill it in for every single operator when when we're going live.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer: transcript says the teams may need to work out how; no assignment was made.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [The group] Provide Vertical Icons: Select and provide the desired icons for separating vertical sections in the interface.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um if you want to give me the icons that you'd like to use to separate these ones uh we can easily add those in as well.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer: a conditional offer from Kobi, not an agreed action.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: [Kobi] Prepare rep field information: Configure the player, operator, and partner information fields within the rep view to ensure they are ready for the go live phase.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So I think this one maybe uh we should like take a look this week as well um and prep before go live.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer and misattributed: Kobi suggested both teams take a look; fields are not yet defined and no owner was assigned.

notes: Invite list also includes Marc Cabantog and Miko Sumagang (not heard in transcript). One personnel/onboarding passage (new team member introduction, ~lines 124-138) skipped under rule 5. Meeting time taken from local file name. Several ASR errors (Kobe=Kobi, choice=Joyce, Will=Waleed, dealer assignment=deal assignment). No Jira keys spoken.
